pairs.why: Both show the player from above at a tilt, but B's earbuds are enlarged in the foreground, which exaggerates perspective more than the real card's small earbuds do.
B turns slightly further toward a corner view and shows more of the top opening and coin pile, which is closer to the real chest's high three-quarter view, though both still sit on a low horizon.
A reads as a high three-quarter view on a floor that fades into the backdrop, like the real chair, while B's sharp table edge and corner give an odd, inconsistent ground plane.
The real map is seen from high up with the top face dominant and mild perspective, and B's higher camera shows more of the top face than A's lower, softer-draped view.
A has a turned three-quarter view with the seat top showing and a floor shadow, close to the real chair, while B sits lower and more frontal.
A pushes a wide-angle look, with the grille huge in the foreground and the rails converging hard, while B has milder, more compact perspective like the real cards.
A is turned three-quarter with the boot opening and top visible, like the real cards' high-ish views, while B is a flat side profile that shows no top face.
B uses a three-quarter front view with a simple ground and background, like the real taxi, while A's boxy rover on a gray lunar ground feels more like a technical product view.
